vulnerability.title: Ensure PAM Enforces Password Requirements - Enforce for root User
vulnerability.description: The pam_pwquality module's enforce_for_root parameter controls requirements for enforcing password complexity for the root user. Enable the enforce_for_root setting in /etc/security/pwquality.conf to require the root user to use complex passwords.
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core && { rpm --quiet -q libpwquality; }; then if [ -e "/etc/security/pwquality.conf" ] ; then LC_ALL=C sed -i "/^\s*enforce_for_root/Id" "/etc/security/pwquality.conf" else touch "/etc/security/pwquality.conf" fi # make sure file has newline at the end sed -i -e '$a\' "/etc/security/pwquality.conf" cp "/etc/security/pwquality.conf" "/etc/security/pwquality.conf.bak" # Insert at the end of the file printf '%s\n' "enforce_for_root" >> "/etc/security/pwquality.conf" # Clean up after ourselves. rm "/etc/security/pwquality.conf.bak" else >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done' fi

triage_decision.reason: Enabling enforce_for_root in /etc/security/pwquality.conf is a standard PAM configuration change that does not affect system boot, networking, or file system integrity. It simply requires root to use a complex password, which is a common hardening practice and unlikely to lock out root access if a password is already set.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: authentication/authorization affected; root password complexity enforcement

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan correctly removes any existing enforce_for_root entry, ensures a newline terminator, backs up the file, and appends a new line to activate enforcement. This should resolve the vulnerability when executed. However, the APPEND line should explicitly set a value (e.g., enforce_for_root=1) to avoid potential ambiguity with the PAM module's parser.
concerns: The appended line lacks an explicit value; most PAM configurations expect key=value syntax.
The script does not validate that sed commands succeeded, which could leave the file in an inconsistent state if an error occurs.
There is no check to confirm that the file is writable and that the backup did not overwrite an existing backup.
The plan doesn’t consider locale or encoding issues that might affect sed pattern matching in some environments.
suggested_improvements: Change the appended line to "enforce_for_root=1" to be explicit.
After backup, verify that the backup exists and is identical to the original before proceeding.
Add a check that the sed delete operation did not fail (e.g., by inspecting exit status).
Consider a more robust backup strategy, such as appending a timestamp to the backup filename.
Add a final verification step that shows the effective PAM configuration (e.g., `pam_auth_update` or reading the file).
